drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find our proposed revisions to establish mutual confidentiality obligations, customary exclusions and permitted disclosures, and clear survival and return provisions. These changes are intended to provide a practical framework for discussions without committing either party to a transaction. Please confirm whether they are acceptable and identify the proposed signatories.

edits.text: 1. PURPOSE; CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. The parties wish to evaluate a potential transaction (the “Purpose”). “Confidential Information” means nonpublic information disclosed by or on behalf of either party to the other in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is marked confidential or reasonably should be understood to be confidential given its nature or the circumstances of disclosure, including analyses reflecting such information. Confidential Information excludes information the receiving party can demonstrate: (a) is or becomes public without breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it without a confidentiality restriction before disclosure; (c) is lawfully received from a third party without a confidentiality restriction; or (d) is independently developed without use of Confidential Information.
edits.name: Purpose and definition

edits.text: 2. MUTUAL CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS. In consideration of the parties’ mutual promises, each party receiving Confidential Information shall use it solely for the Purpose and protect it with at least reasonable care. It may disclose Confidential Information only to its directors, officers, employees, and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Agreement or by professional duties of confidentiality. The receiving party is responsible for their compliance. If disclosure is legally required, the receiving party may disclose only the portion legally required and shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt prior notice and reasonably cooperate, at the disclosing party’s expense, in seeking protective treatment. On written request, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy Confidential Information, except copies required by law, professional recordkeeping obligations, or routine backup systems; retained information remains subject to this Agreement.
edits.name: Mutual obligations

edits.text: 3. TERM; SURVIVAL. This Agreement takes effect on the date of the last signature and remains in effect for twenty-four months, unless earlier terminated by either party on written notice. Confidentiality and use restrictions survive for three years after expiration or termination; for information qualifying as a trade secret, they continue for so long as it remains a trade secret under applicable law. Neither party is obligated to disclose information or proceed with any transaction. No intellectual property rights are granted except the limited right to use Confidential Information for the Purpose.
edits.name: Term and survival

edits.text: 4. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm for which damages may be inadequate. The disclosing party may seek injunctive relief, subject to applicable law and court discretion, in addition to other available remedies.

edits.text: 1. PURPOSE; CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. The parties wish to evaluate a potential transaction (the “Purpose”). “Confidential Information” means nonpublic information disclosed before, on, or after the effective date of this Agreement by or on behalf of either party to the other in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is marked confidential or reasonably should be understood to be confidential given its nature or the circumstances of disclosure, including analyses reflecting such information. The obligations under this Agreement apply from its effective date to all such Confidential Information, including pre-signing disclosures made for the Purpose. Confidential Information excludes information the receiving party can demonstrate: (a) is or becomes public without breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it without a confidentiality restriction before disclosure; (c) is lawfully received from a third party without a confidentiality restriction; or (d) is independently developed without use of Confidential Information.

2. MUTUAL CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS. In consideration of the parties’ mutual promises, each party receiving Confidential Information shall use it solely for the Purpose and protect it with at least reasonable care. It may disclose Confidential Information only to its directors, officers, employees, and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Agreement or by professional duties of confidentiality. The receiving party is responsible for their compliance. If disclosure is legally required, the receiving party may disclose only the portion legally required and shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt prior notice and reasonably cooperate, at the disclosing party’s expense, in seeking protective treatment. On written request, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy Confidential Information, including copies and analyses reflecting it, and, if requested, provide written certification by an authorized representative of compliance with that obligation, identifying any categories of copies retained under the following exceptions. The receiving party may retain copies only to the extent required by applicable law or maintained in routine disaster-recovery backup systems that are not reasonably capable of selective deletion. Retained copies may be accessed only as necessary for legally required retention or disaster recovery, and not for the Purpose or any other business use. Any copies restored for disaster recovery shall promptly be deleted when no longer necessary for that recovery, unless retention is required by law. All retained copies remain subject to the confidentiality and use restrictions of this Agreement for as long as they are retained.

3. TERM; SURVIVAL. This Agreement takes effect on the date of the last signature and remains in effect for twenty-four months, unless earlier terminated by either party on written notice. Confidentiality and use restrictions survive for five years after expiration or termination; for information qualifying as a trade secret, they continue for so long as it remains a trade secret under applicable law. The obligations applicable to retained copies under Section 2 continue for as long as those copies are retained. Neither party is obligated to disclose information or proceed with any transaction. No intellectual property rights are granted except the limited right to use Confidential Information for the Purpose.

4. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm for which damages may be inadequate. The disclosing party may seek injunctive relief, subject to applicable law and court discretion, in addition to other available remedies.

5. GOVERNING LAW; JURISDICTION. This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts located in New York County, New York, and the federal courts located in that county, and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum.
